title: LLM Content Moderation and User Satisfaction: Evidence from Response Refusals in Chatbot Arena

live_model.evidence: Sec. 3.2: "we conducted a validation using GPT-4-turbo as a second annotator. The model was instructed to classify all 3,500 responses ... in a zero-shot setting."

prompt.note: The five-category zero-shot classification scheme is described narratively (Sec. 3.2); no verbatim prompt template is printed and there is no prompt appendix in the paper.

claim.metric: none for the live id (GPT-4-turbo used only as a second annotator to validate human labels, not as the studied classifier)

data.source: Chatbot Arena conversation pairs (49,938 one-turn pairs); refusal classifier and hand-labeled dataset released on HuggingFace (Human-CentricAI/LLM-Refusal-Classifier and llm-refusal-chatbot-arena)

notes: Krippendorff's Alpha (0.668) and Cohen's Kappa (0.67) are reported for GPT-4-turbo vs. human agreement (Sec. 3.2), but this is an inter-annotator reliability check, not a task-performance claim for the model itself; the paper's main results (Tables 4-6) are all from the fine-tuned RoBERTa classifier.
